To inform users to monitor equipment operation and condition, and to identify the onset, occurrence, and effects of aft
end compressor rubs (when the tip of the rotor blade rubs the casing).  Rubs are evident when blade tip material is
adversely affected. Information in this TIL is supplemental to information in the Inspection and Maintenance Manual
provided with the gas turbine.
To update the technical content of the TIL, including frequency of tip loss and recommendations when discovered.

The compressor section of F-Class gas turbines has 18
(0-17) stages of rotating components (rotor blades) and
stationary components (stator vanes).

Some F-class machines have experienced aft end
compressor rubs. These rubs range from light scoring
on the casing to material loss at the blade tip. This
phenomenon was concluded to be very low risk
relative to unit operation and reliability. No
performance impact and no forced outages have been
experienced as a result. Rotor blades in rows 13, 14,
and 15 are primarily affected.

elements.description: A cross-section diagram shows a series of vertical and horizontal lines, with two highlighted pink rectangles in the lower center.

elements.content:
Based on the conclusion of Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
and fleet experience, aft end rubs are primarily induced
because of frequent restarts between two (2) to eight
(8) hours after shutdown. During this transient period,
the thermal compression of the casing relative to the
rotor can decrease clearances and can lead to rubs
upon restart. The heat generated from a rub can lower
the local material fatigue strength of the blade
resulting in material tip loss in the event of another rub.
Typical material loss dimensions are less than
1/16 inch2 in area (see Figure 2).

elements.description: A green, rectangular object is positioned above a circular image with an arrow pointing towards a labeled section.

elements.content:
Restarting a unit 2 to 8 hours after a shutdown or trip is
within the operating envelope, but this may cause rubs
in some cases. Aft end rubs and/or tip loss pose very
low risk to unit operation and reliability. No
performance impact and no forced outages have been
experienced due to this issue.

Follow operating practices per GER 3620 to reduce the
potential for rubs on aft end compressor blades. In
addition to the GER 3620 guidelines, the following
recommendations would also help minimize aft end
rubs and tip loss occurrence.

â€¢ Keep enclosure doors closed during
startup, shutdown and normal operation.

â€¢ Be aware that restarting the gas turbine between two (2) and eight (8) hours following a shutdown or trip will cause the clearances in the aft end to decrease. If the unit operates this way now or has in the past, there is a potential for this clearance closure to cause aft end tip rubs. As a result, the area should be included in the yearly borescope inspections.

â€¢ Eliminate any potential pipe leaks that may cause
quenching of the gas turbine compressor
discharge casing.

â€¢ Ensure vent fans and exhaust fans to the gas turbine enclosure are functioning properly such
that no local forced convection is taking place at or
near the compressor discharge casing.

â€¢ Integrate the inspection for aft end compressor rubs with your yearly scheduled borescope inspection per GER 3620. Observe rotor blade stages 13 through 17 and look for mushroomed material (see Figure 3), bluing at the blade tip,
and / or markings in the casing area.

elements.content:
If rubs or tip loss do occur, blending to increase clearances can be performed at Major Inspections (MI)
or when the Compressor Discharge Casing (CDC) is
removed. During repairs, clearances of rotor blades can
be increased radially by tip grinding and polishing, and
tip corners repaired by blade blending. Typically, 20
mils radially of material can be removed to both
increase clearance and remove heat affected and
rolled over material.

Following this operation, a penetrant inspection must
be performed to ensure no tip cracks are present. If
the CDC is removed prior to the major inspection,
clearances can also be increased to eliminate the
potential for tip rubs should the customer desire.
Please contact your local GE service representative for
assistance.

â€¢ Trained GE Borescope technician to perform
borescope inspection, approximately eight (8)
hours.

â€¢ Trained GE Blade technician for rotor blade
clearance increases, approximately 16 hours once
the casing has been removed.
